question: Should memory-core add default-on user-scoped memory isolation through this new `memory.isolation` config surface, or should the work be narrowed under the open memory partition tracker first?
rationale: This changes a privacy boundary, persistent memory layout, QMD state scoping, and config defaults; automation can identify defects, but maintainers must choose the supported product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Require a narrowed security-reviewed fix
options.body: Keep the PR open only if it fixes the default/options contract, adds upgrade-compatible behavior, and provides real two-user builtin and QMD proof before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the broader config surface
options.body: A maintainer can approve the new config shape, but then the PR needs docs, tests, and proof for every accepted option and the default upgrade path.

options.title: Pause in favor of the tracker
options.body: If the direction is not ready, close or pause this branch and continue design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63550.

recommendation.title: Require a narrowed security-reviewed fix
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open only if it fixes the default/options contract, adds upgrade-compatible behavior, and provides real two-user builtin and QMD proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the freshest current-main history on the memory-core and host SDK paths that would carry this decision.
